why: Flaky test fix in today's tooling, test code only (0036). named() in scripts/typecheck.integration.test.ts no longer polls pgrep for the stand-in compiler's start under a 5 s wall clock. The stand-in prints 'ready' on a pipe after it has written its name back, named() awaits that line through the child's own stdout event (and fails at once if the child errors or exits first), then checks pgrep -x once with the same assertion. The 5 s bound in until() is unchanged and no assertion was dropped. The other waits in the file read the system under test's own output (the events file the typecheck's compiler writes, its stderr, its exit), so they stay as they are.
note: The law file is .integration. and spawns processes, so it was not run on the laptop; the change was reasoned from the code. Ran pnpm format, pnpm lint and one pnpm typecheck. PR 1506 (the typecheck port) edits the same lines of named.mjs and named(), so the two conflict and the second to land takes the other's change.
